item.title: Kanazawa Castle & Gyokusen-inmaru Garden: Seat of the Powerful Maeda Clan — Guide
item.description: Kanazawa Castle was once the seat of the Maeda clan, rulers of the Kaga domain and the wealthiest feudal domain in Japan during the Edo period, though the original castle structure was lost to repeated fires over the centuries and much of what visitors see today is careful modern reconstruction using traditional techniques. Adjacent to the castle grounds, the Gyokusen-inmaru Garden was restored and reopened in 2015 after being rediscovered through historical research, offering a quieter garden counterpart to the crowds at nearby Kenrokuen.

item.title: Maruoka Castle: One of Japan's Oldest Surviving Castle Keeps — Guide
item.description: Maruoka Castle was built in 1576 and its keep is considered one of the oldest surviving original castle structures in Japan, having survived centuries of conflict, fire and the widespread castle demolitions of the Meiji era that destroyed many of the country’s original fortifications. Unlike the larger, more elaborate reconstructed castles found elsewhere in Japan, Maruoka’s modest, sturdy keep with its distinctive stone-tiled roof offers visitors a rare, authentic look at genuine Sengoku-period castle architecture, and the surrounding park is a popular local cherry blossom spot each spring.
